environment.browserSurface: Google Chrome controlled through the installed browser extension

checks.observed: axe-core 4.12.1 reported zero selected WCAG 2 A, AA, 2.1 AA, and 2.2 AA rule violations and zero incomplete checks at a 1265 by 513 application viewport.
axe-core 4.12.1 reported zero selected-rule violations and zero incomplete checks at a 360 by 844 application viewport.
At the narrow breakpoint, the application document measured 360 CSS pixels for both client width and scroll width; the main heading and navigation landmarks remained present.
A direct URL with view=incidents, the current incident ID, and tab=timeline selected the intended closed incident and exposed its 38-entry timeline without prior in-app navigation.
End selected Post-incident review, Home selected Summary, ArrowRight selected Timeline, and ArrowLeft returned to Summary; aria-selected and the tab query parameter remained synchronized.
Chrome Back restored Timeline and Chrome Forward restored Summary while the selected tab and tab query parameter remained synchronized.
The declare-incident dialog initially focused its close control; Escape closed the dialog and returned focus to the Declare incident button.
At the requested 375 by 844 window size, opening the navigation drawer focused its close control; Escape closed the drawer and returned focus to the open-navigation control with aria-expanded=false.
Chrome recorded no warning or error entries during the final local application and accessibility checks.

limitations: This is an internal controlled browser check, not formal independent human QA or external-user evidence.
The accessibility scan covered selected axe WCAG rules; it does not establish complete WCAG conformance or replace keyboard-only and screen-reader testing by people.
Only one browser engine and synthetic local data were exercised; Safari, Firefox, real mobile devices, hosted identity, HTTPS edge behavior, staging, and production were not tested.

The accessibility harness removed frame and content-security-policy restrictions only on its loopback proxy so axe could inspect the document. The actual Worker security headers were tested separately and were not weakened.
The narrow-layout overflow conclusion is a DOM measurement in one emulated viewport, not a cross-device laboratory measurement.
This run did not repeat the earlier two-tab polling exercise; API, state-transition, and load behavior were verified separately against the same Worker artifact.
